chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
When you gain power over your adversary, make pardon towards him an expression of gratitude for the ability to overpower him.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of forgiving an enemy when you have power over them?
ai.summary: In this maxim from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elevates forgiveness from a passive restraint to an active spiritual practice, framing the capacity to punish as a divine trust rather than a personal right. This perspective aligns with the Shia emphasis on *shukr* (gratitude) for blessings, where the believer acknowledges that true power lies in mastering one's ego through magnanimity. It serves as a practical guide for leaders and individuals to transform potential vengeance into an act of worship, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of *'afw* (pardon) over *'iqab* (punishment).

en.sayed-ali-raza: 11. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
When you gain power over your adversary pardon him by way of thanks for being able to overpower him. [1]
